measured_time.note: These measurements apply to this local development run. Warm requests can benefit from caching; they are not cold-start throughput estimates.

findings.note: All three answer responses are identical. All three metrics pass on each repeat, giving 3/3 automated quality passes.

The model repeats 15 instead of acknowledging insufficient context. The passage supplies a ranking cutoff, not the total number requested. Correctness, groundedness and the exact-abstention check fail on every repeat. Relevancy grades vary despite identical case inputs and responses; the statement-extraction and verdict-request prompt hashes match across repeats, while the final explanation prompt reflects different verdicts. The later relevancy explanations also mix relevancy with missing evidence.

The actual response is exactly 09:00 on all three repeats and matches a reference and the supplied policy. The correctness prompt hash is identical on all three repeats. The first judge result invents the typo 09:0:0 and assigns zero; later results assign ten before DeepEval normalizes them to 1.0, but retain contradictory typo language in their reasons. Raw output scores and normalization were verified. This is observed judge-output variability for the same grading prompt, not changed answer text.

interpretation: All three selected cases have exactly repeated answer text under the fixed baseline settings. Automated trial outcomes are 5 passes and 4 flags, with one case passing every repeat. These are not model-accuracy estimates: they combine genuine answer failures with judge grading problems. The small, already-inspected pilot subset, repeated observations, shared model-family bias and pending genuine human validation limit generalization. No cause of the judge variability has been established.
